title: Simulation of a Nondeterministic Register Program
statement: Fix nonnegative integers $m,d,k_D$, sets $\Lambda,SD$, an input bit string $x$, a nondeterministic register program $A$ with $m$ registers and $d$ oracle choices, an initial location $l_0$, an oracle, a deterministic $k_D$-tape machine $D$, initial decider states $q_0(j)$, and bounds $B,W$. For every $N\ge 0$, location $l\in\Lambda$, register valuation $v:\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\to\mathbb N$, and output bit string $\mathrm{out}$, suppose every length-$N$ choice string makes the program halt from configuration $(l,v,\text{no answer})$, and every configuration before halting satisfies the guard requiring the deterministic preconditions and the register bit-length bounds by $W$. Then there is a time $T$ such that, from the compiled machine configuration corresponding to $(l,v,\mathrm{out})$, every choice string of length at most $T$ yields a configuration whose first $m$ work-tape heads stay between $-1$ and $W$ and whose remaining work-tape heads stay within distance $B$ of zero; every choice string of length exactly $T$ yields a halting configuration whose output is $\mathrm{out}$ followed by an answer attainable by the register program in $N$ choices. Moreover, for every answer attainable by the register program in $N$ choices, some length-$T$ choice string makes the compiled machine output $\mathrm{out}$ followed by that answer.
